question: Why might a woman get a positive home pregnancy test even if she is not actually carrying a healthy pregnancy?

options.A: Normal stress levels can trick the urine test strip into changing colors
options.B: Expired test kits always show two lines regardless of hormone levels
options.C: Drinking too much water before the test changes the chemical pH balance
options.D: Certain rare tumors or abnormal tissue growths can also produce hCG hormone

explanation: Because rare conditions can also pump out hCG, lab tests remain categorized as probable signs rather than absolute positive signs. Brilliant clinical thinking!

question: Why is tertiary care considered the highest tier in the health system?

options.A: It is the only level permitted to provide routine childhood immunizations
options.B: It completely replaces the need for community health centers
options.C: It offers highly specialized sub-specialists and advanced medical technology
options.D: It focuses exclusively on basic health education and disease prevention

explanation: Great thinking! Tertiary centers like teaching hospitals are where you find advanced equipment and experts tackling the most complex medical cases.

question: A patient has been on a strict low-fat diet for months. Which sign might point to a vitamin deficiency?

options.A: Easy bruising and prolonged bleeding times from vitamin K lack
options.B: Yellow discoloration of the skin from excess beta-carotene
options.C: Sudden swelling of the lower extremities due to excess sodium
options.D: Severe dental decay caused by rapid loss of enamel

explanation: Well done! Vitamin K helps blood clot. Without enough fat absorption, a deficiency can lead to easy bruising and bleeding.

question: When would a nurse most likely need to check a primary literature source?

options.A: When looking up the standard adult dose of paracetamol for a headache
options.B: When checking the common side effects of routine oral antibiotics
options.C: When searching for newly published clinical trial results on a novel cancer drug
options.D: When verifying the route of administration for an intravenous fluid

explanation: Exactly! Primary sources are original research studies. You go to them when you need the absolute newest, raw findings that haven't made it into textbooks yet.

question: What physical sign in the inner eyelids or nail beds is a classic warning sign of possible anemia?

options.A: Erythema
options.B: Jaundice
options.C: Pallor
options.D: Cyanosis

explanation: Spot on! Pale (pallor) inner eyelids and nail beds tell us hemoglobin levels might be low, which is a classic sign of anemia.

question: Why is clear, objective nursing documentation so crucial in skilled care facilities?

options.A: It is only used by insurance companies to deny resident coverage.
options.B: It guarantees that no resident will ever experience a fall.
options.C: It serves as a legal safeguard and proves that skilled criteria were met.
options.D: It replaces the need for verbal shift handovers between nurses.

explanation: Good charting is your best friend! It acts as a legal proof that the resident truly needed and received expert nursing care.

question: When a registered nurse delegates a task to a junior colleague, who remains ultimately accountable?

options.A: The hospital chief medical director
options.B: The registered nurse who delegated the task
options.C: The junior staff member who performed the task
options.D: The patient's family members

explanation: Delegating a task shares the physical work, but as the RN, you keep the overall accountability to ensure it was done safely.

question: A healthy pregnant patient in her third trimester complains of feeling slightly short of breath during normal daily tasks. What is the best initial nursing interpretation?

options.A: This suggests the fetus is not getting enough air and needs immediate delivery
options.B: This points to a severe pulmonary infection that must be treated with antibiotics
options.C: This indicates early heart failure and requires immediate emergency oxygen therapy
options.D: This is a normal physiological adaptation caused by the enlarged uterus and hormonal changes

explanation: Elevated progesterone and upward pressure from the uterus naturally cause mild dyspnea without indicating actual disease. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T003#GNS226_U2_T003_h2)

question: How do you place AED pads on a patient who has a pacemaker lump on their upper left chest?

options.A: Place the AED pad at least one inch away from the device
options.B: Refuse to use the AED because implanted devices block shocks entirely
options.C: Disable the pacemaker using a magnet before applying the pads
options.D: Place the AED pad directly over the bulge to improve shock delivery

explanation: Just place the pad about an inch away from the pacemaker bulge. If you put it right on top, it can absorb the shock energy and damage the implanted device.

question: What is a major difference between paracetamol (acetaminophen) and NSAIDs?

options.A: Acetaminophen causes significant gastric bleeding
options.B: NSAIDs work exclusively inside the spinal cord
options.C: NSAIDs have no effect on body temperature
options.D: Acetaminophen lacks peripheral anti-inflammatory action

explanation: Both lower fever and ease pain, but paracetamol doesn't fight body inflammation or affect bleeding the way NSAIDs do.

question: What is the biggest weakness of using the rational (logical) method by itself?

options.A: It cannot be written down on paper or spoken aloud
options.B: It ignores all forms of mathematical calculation
options.C: A flawed starting premise leads to an incorrect conclusion
options.D: It takes too many years to complete a single calculation

explanation: Logic is only as good as its starting point. If your first assumption is wrong, your final answer will be wrong too!

question: On a partograph, what does it mean if labour progress crosses the "alert line"?

options.A: Labour is progressing slowly and requires closer observation
options.B: Immediate surgical delivery is mandatory right this second
options.C: The baby has already been successfully delivered
options.D: The mother's blood pressure is completely normal

explanation: Think of the alert line as a friendly tap on the shoulder—it tells us labour is slowing down a bit, so we need to watch mum more closely.

question: Why is receiving feedback from a tertiary center important for a primary care nurse?

options.A: It allows the primary nurse to take over the role of a specialist doctor
options.B: It reduces the workload at the local clinic to zero
options.C: It builds professional confidence and improves ongoing management of the client
options.D: It stops the client from ever needing medication refills again

explanation: Getting feedback closes the loop! It helps primary nurses learn from specialist outcomes and grow more confident in managing similar cases.

question: Why do patients with severe fluid overload often develop crackling sounds in their lungs?

options.A: Dehydration causes the bronchial tubes to narrow and whistle
options.B: Fluid backs up into the pulmonary air sacs and airways
options.C: The chest muscles weaken from holding extra body weight
options.D: The patient develops a secondary bacterial pneumonia infection

explanation: Spot on! When the plumbing system is overloaded, fluid backs up into the tiny air sacs (alveoli) in the lungs, making a crackling sound when they breathe.

question: What postnatal sign shows that the uterus is slow to shrink back down to its normal pre-pregnancy size?

options.A: Increased breast engorgement
options.B: Elevated maternal temperature
options.C: Uterine subinvolution
options.D: Rapid lochia cessation

explanation: Subinvolution is just a medical term for when the womb takes way too long to go back to its normal size and tone, often leading to longer-than-normal bleeding.

question: A patient recovering from a large surgical wound requires tissue repair. Which macronutrient should the nurse ensure is adequately provided?

options.A: Carbohydrates
options.B: Fats
options.C: Proteins
options.D: Water

explanation: Proteins supply the amino acids required to build new tissue and heal surgical wounds effectively. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T015#GNS227_U2_T015_h2)

question: Who founded the Henry Street Settlement to help shape early visiting nursing in urban America?

options.A: Mary Seacole
options.B: Clara Barton
options.C: Florence Nightingale
options.D: Lillian Wald

explanation: Lillian Wald was a true public health pioneer who started the Henry Street Settlement to bring proper healthcare to people living in crowded city tenements.

question: Why must nurses carefully separate normal aging from disease pathology?

options.A: To prove that biological aging can be completely reversed with rest
options.B: To determine the exact financial cost of long-term hospital admission
options.C: To ensure that older adults never receive any prescription medications
options.D: To avoid treating normal age-related changes as if they are illnesses

explanation: Knowing what changes are a natural part of growing older prevents unnecessary medical interventions and helps nurses focus true care where it is needed. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T8#GNS225_U5_T8_h1)

question: What is the main job of a pharmacological antagonist?

options.A: It replaces the liver enzymes completely
options.B: It mimics the exact action of a natural hormone
options.C: It stimulates maximum receptor activity
options.D: It blocks the effect of an agonist

explanation: Think of an antagonist as a blocker! It attaches to a cell receptor site without turning it on, which stops agonists from coming in and doing their thing. You've got this!

question: What is the main purpose of body cavities in human anatomy?

options.A: To produce hormones for metabolic balance
options.B: To digest nutrients absorbed from food
options.C: To pump blood throughout the body systems
options.D: To protect and support internal organs

explanation: Body cavities act as safe, enclosed spaces that cushion internal organs against physical trauma. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T3#GNS111_U1_T3_h1)

question: Why is community participation important for making public health spending more transparent?

options.A: It empowers local citizens to hold health authorities accountable for funds
options.B: It removes the need for trained accountants in hospitals
options.C: It allows villagers to write the national health budget themselves
options.D: It guarantees that private clinics will lower their drug prices

explanation: When the local community is involved, they can ask questions and make sure that money meant for their local clinic actually gets used there.

question: What is the main purpose of looking at clinical signs in tummy (gastrointestinal) problems?

options.A: To calculate the total hospital bill for the patient
options.B: To replace all lab tests and scans completely
options.C: To guess the exact day the patient will leave the hospital
options.D: To give us clues about how well the gut is working and looking

explanation: Signs and symptoms act like windows into the digestive tract, helping nurses and doctors figure out what is going wrong inside.

question: What does the term 'digital divide' mean in modern healthcare?

options.A: The difference between paper medical records and electronic health records
options.B: Disagreements between doctors and nurses over which software program to use
options.C: Inequality in access to technology and internet services among different populations
options.D: The technical separation between hospital database servers and clinic computers

explanation: The digital divide happens when some patients lack smartphones, computers, or good internet, making it hard for them to use telehealth services. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h6)

question: Why should nursing researchers care about national and global health goals?

options.A: It helps secure research funding and ensures the study addresses urgent needs
options.B: It removes all ethical considerations from the research process
options.C: It eliminates the requirement to collect informed consent from patients
options.D: It guarantees that no other nurse will ever read the published paper

explanation: When your research tackles pressing real-world problems, it's easier to get support and make a true difference in society.

question: Why is tracking unexpected weight changes so important during an outpatient checkup?

options.A: It measures the exact amount of water a person drinks
options.B: It calculates the exact vitamin levels in the bloodstream
options.C: It proves the client is exercising vigorously every day
options.D: It is a key indicator of underlying nutritional risk

explanation: Great thinking! Sudden, unplanned weight loss is often a red flag that points to malnutrition or a hidden health issue.

question: Why do symptoms suddenly show up after a quiet incubation phase?

options.A: The number of germs and body damage cross a tipping point
options.B: The immune system completely stops working
options.C: The germs suddenly turn into a completely different species
options.D: Medicines taken by the patient start fighting healthy cells

explanation: Illness only becomes visible when the growing number of germs and tiny injuries finally overwhelm the body's natural defenses. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T84#GNS214_U1_T84_h2)

question: Why are daily full-body soap baths usually not recommended for frail elderly patients?

options.A: Elderly patients are completely immune to body odors
options.B: Water damages their internal organs through the skin pores
options.C: Their skin loses natural oils and becomes dry and irritated
options.D: Soap makes their bones become fragile and brittle

explanation: As skin ages, it makes fewer natural oils. Daily harsh soap and scrubbing can strip away what's left, leading to painful, dry, cracked skin.

question: How do nurses accurately measure fluid output from a heavy surgical dressing or pad?

options.A: Estimating the stain size using a common ruler
options.B: Squeezing the fluid out into a measuring cup
options.C: Asking the patient how much fluid they think leaked
options.D: Weighing the wet item and subtracting the dry weight

explanation: Weight is the most reliable way to quantify fluid soaked into solid materials, where one gram roughly equals one milliliter. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T19#GNS122_U1_T19_h5)

question: Which clinical sign is commonly seen in someone with severely low calcium (hypocalcemia)?

options.A: Fruity breath odor and deep rapid breathing
options.B: Positive Trousseau's and Chvostek's signs
options.C: Profound hyperpigmentation of the skin
options.D: Exophthalmos and a fine hand tremor

explanation: Calcium keeps our nerves and muscles calm. When calcium drops too low, nerves become super jumpy, causing muscles to twitch or spasm during Trousseau's and Chvostek's tests.

question: Why does a peri-operative nurse need both strong clinical skills and great communication?

options.A: Operating rooms prohibit verbal communication during procedures.
options.B: The nursing council mandates dual certification for all surgical staff.
options.C: Patients face high physical risks and emotional stress during surgery.
options.D: Surgeons require nurses to manage hospital administrative duties.

explanation: Surgery is a big deal! Patients and their families go through a lot of physical and emotional stress, so nurses need to be skilled and comforting.

question: At what exact stage is a secondary oocyte frozen right when ovulation happens?

options.A: Telophase of meiosis II
options.B: Metaphase of meiosis II
options.C: Anaphase of meiosis I
options.D: Prophase of meiosis I

explanation: When the egg is released, it is paused again—this time in metaphase of meiosis II. It will only wake up if a sperm comes along!

question: A nurse manager wants to reduce medication handover delays. What is the best action during the Plan phase?

options.A: Decide on a specific new handover format and plan who will test it on the morning shift
options.B: Wait for a major audit to tell the ward whether their handovers are too slow
options.C: Fire the nurses who take too long during their shift change reports
options.D: Immediately order all nurses to stop talking during handovers starting today

explanation: Spot on! Good planning means picking a specific idea and testing it on a single shift before making big changes.

question: What is the main goal of descriptive statistics in a study?

options.A: Summarize the basic features and scores of the sample data
options.B: Replace the need for taking patient medical histories
options.C: Prove that a new drug cures a disease in all humans
options.D: Determine the financial cost of running a hospital ward

explanation: Descriptive statistics give you a quick, clear snapshot of what your sample looks like using simple summaries like averages and percentages.

question: What is actually happening inside the body during the incubation period of an infection?

options.A: The patient is experiencing the peak severity of organ inflammation
options.B: Body tissues are undergoing rapid repair after the infection clears
options.C: The immune system is actively clearing the pathogen from the blood
options.D: The pathogen is multiplying inside the host before symptoms appear

explanation: During the incubation period, the germ is quietly building up numbers inside the body. The patient feels completely fine—for now!

question: In a busy ward, what do we mean by 'alarm fatigue'?

options.A: The batteries dying in portable monitoring gadgets
options.B: The machine sensors wearing out after long use
options.C: Getting so used to constant beeps that staff start ignoring them
options.D: A power cut that shuts off all bedside monitors

explanation: When too many false or minor alarms go off, nurses can become desensitized. That's why managing alarm settings safely is a vital nursing skill!

question: During a vaginal exam, a student midwife feels the baby's skull bones overlapping tightly with no way to separate them. How is this charted?

options.A: Grade 2 or Grade 3 moulding
options.B: Normal physiological shift
options.C: Caput succedaneum score
options.D: Grade 0 normal molding

explanation: When bones overlap firmly and won't budge, that's advanced moulding (Grade 2 or 3). It's a key sign to watch out for to prevent prolonged or blocked labour!

question: What is the primary purpose of using a bowel diary for a patient with incontinence?

options.A: To test the chemical pH of passing stool
options.B: To track patterns of leakage, food intake, and bowel movements
options.C: To measure the exact length of the large intestine
options.D: To replace the need for a physical examination

explanation: A bowel diary provides concrete daily records of when and why accidents happen, helping nurses and doctors plan targeted interventions. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T8#GNS212_U1_T8_h5)

question: What are nutrients mainly known as in nursing care?

options.A: Caloric restrictions required for managing chronic weight loss
options.B: Chemical substances in food needed for body function and repair
options.C: Medical supplements prescribed only during surgical recovery
options.D: Artificial additives used to preserve packaged hospital meals

explanation: You got this! Nutrients are simply the useful components in our food that give our bodies energy and help us grow and heal every day.

question: How can rural communities creatively solve the problem of getting sick patients to a clinic?

options.A: Organizing local emergency transport systems like tricycles
options.B: Waiting for ambulances to be stationed in every street
options.C: Demanding that the government buy cars for every family
options.D: Building major federal highways to connect every village

explanation: Spot on! Communities often band together to arrange local transport like branded tricycles or bikes to bridge the gap during emergencies.

question: Which of these actions is a big NO-DO (contraindicated) for a venomous snakebite?

options.A: Positioning the limb at or below heart level
options.B: Transporting the patient to a medical facility promptly
options.C: Applying a tight tourniquet to the bitten limb
options.D: Keeping the patient calm and resting quietly

explanation: Never use a tight tourniquet! It cuts off blood flow completely, causing tissue death. Keep the limb calm and get the patient to the hospital safely.

question: What is the very first priority when a patient arrives in the emergency department with a severe laceration?

options.A: Checking airway, breathing, and circulation
options.B: Administering local anesthesia
options.C: Choosing the right suture material
options.D: Cleaning the wound with iodine

explanation: General patient stability and life-threatening issues always come before treating localized injuries like skin lacerations. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T3#GNS311_U4_T3_h1)

question: Who founded the Henry Street Settlement and coined the term public health nurse?

options.A: Clara Barton
options.B: Florence Nightingale
options.C: Mary Seacole
options.D: Lillian Wald

explanation: Lillian Wald established the Henry Street Settlement in New York City, which became a foundational model for modern public health nursing. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T6#GNS225_U1_T6_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a major challenge facing formal home health care in Nigeria?

options.A: Inadequate road infrastructure slowing down nurse transit
options.B: Universal government funding covering all home care services
options.C: Shortage of a unified national health policy for home care
options.D: Public preference for traditional healing methods in some areas

explanation: Universal government funding for home care doesn't exist here yet! Most people pay out-of-pocket, making funding a major hurdle, not a reality.

question: In traditional Nigerian societies, what was usually believed to be the main cause of severe mental illness?

options.A: Degeneration of brain cells from aging
options.B: A deficiency of essential dietary vitamins
options.C: Spiritual forces and ancestral influences
options.D: Genetic mutations passed down generations

explanation: Spot on! Historically, communities often connected deep emotional or psychological struggles to spiritual factors, witchcraft, or broken taboos rather than biological causes. You've got this!

question: You need to add more water to a running steam generator. What is your very first step?

options.A: Ask the parent to hold the steam nozzle away
options.B: Pour cold water slowly while the unit is still boiling
options.C: Turn off and unplug the unit before adding water
options.D: Cover the hot metal parts with a dry towel first

explanation: Always power down and unplug first! This protects you from electrical shocks and nasty steam burns.

question: A young student in Nigeria worries that taking Postinor-2 will make her barren. How should you respond?

options.A: Prescribe a strong surgical procedure to clear her reproductive system
options.B: Scold her for engaging in premarital sex and refuse to give her the medication
options.C: Gently educate her with facts, explaining that the drug does not cause permanent infertility
options.D: Agree with her fears and advise her never to use any form of family planning

explanation: Market myths can be scary! Gently talking clients through the facts builds trust and ensures they get safe, accurate reproductive healthcare. You're going to be an amazing nurse!

question: A community health nurse opens a delivery kit and finds a soap bar, a plastic sheet, a cord tie, a razor blade, and a cloth. What is the primary role of the razor blade?

options.A: To open other plastic packaging
options.B: To rupture the amniotic sac
options.C: To clean the mother's skin
options.D: To cut the umbilical cord

explanation: The razor blade serves as the sterile instrument dedicated to cutting the umbilical cord cleanly. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T10#GNS225_U2_T10_h2)

question: A newly qualified staff nurse guides a student on proper wound dressing technique. What does this situation demonstrate?

options.A: Formal ward management
options.B: Strict administrative control
options.C: Delegation of illegal tasks
options.D: Everyday nursing leadership

explanation: Guiding and teaching colleagues during clinical care is a form of leadership that any nurse can and should practice. [learn more](GST321_U3_T3#GST321_U3_T3_h1)

question: What is the main sign that sets a food-borne intoxication apart from an infection?

options.A: Living parasites in the blood
options.B: Rapid onset of symptoms within hours
options.C: A long incubation period lasting weeks
options.D: High persistent fever as the very first sign

explanation: Because intoxications are caused by toxins already sitting in the food, your body reacts super fast—often within hours! You're crushing this.

question: What exactly is a pure culture?

options.A: An agar plate covered in twenty different types of bacteria
options.B: A liquid broth that has been filtered to remove all water
options.C: A culture containing only a single species of microorganism
options.D: A water sample taken from a deep underground well

explanation: Great job! A pure culture holds just one type of organism, making it easy to study its unique traits without distractions.

question: Why must a patient empty their bladder right before getting a paracentesis?

options.A: To lower the patient's blood pressure safely
options.B: To prevent accidental puncture of the bladder
options.C: To prevent the patient from feeling dizzy
options.D: To make the urine sample easier to collect

explanation: A full bladder gets pushed up and is way too easy to accidentally nick with the needle. Safety first!

question: A patient from a large extended family is admitted to the ward. What are you most likely to observe?

options.A: Complete isolation with zero visitors due to strict rules
options.B: Immediate legal action to discharge the patient
options.C: Many relatives visiting, offering opinions, and sharing caregiving duties
options.D: Total reliance on hospital staff for basic feeding and hygiene tasks

explanation: In Nigeria, extended families are wonderfully close-knit and rally round to support a sick member during hospitalization.

question: What should a nurse do immediately after finding abnormal, life-threatening changes during an exam?

options.A: Delete the entry from the computer to avoid alarming others
options.B: Ask the patient to walk around the room to see if it improves
options.C: Report the findings to the physician or charge nurse right away
options.D: Wait until the shift change report to mention it to anyone

explanation: Critical changes require prompt communication and action to ensure the patient gets emergency medical intervention quickly. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h7)

question: Why is nurse-led education for patients and visitors important for waste management?

options.A: To train family members how to incinerate trash in the hospital yard
options.B: To encourage visitors to bring their own waste bags from home
options.C: To prevent visitors from accidentally touching hazardous waste or opening bins
options.D: To reduce the hospital budget spent on buying cleaning detergents

explanation: Visitors often do not know clinical waste risks, so nursing guidance keeps them from touching contaminated materials. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h7)

question: In infectious disease, what exactly is a 'vector'?

options.A: A chemical spray used to clean operating theatre floors
options.B: An inanimate object like a door handle that carries bacteria
options.C: A specialized blood test used to diagnose viral infections
options.D: A living organism that transmits a pathogen from one host to another

explanation: Think of mosquitoes or ticks! Vectors are living creatures that carry germs from one person or animal to another.

question: What is the main goal of 'sensate focus' exercises in sex therapy?

options.A: To replace all forms of verbal communication between partners
options.B: To test the physical endurance of the cardiovascular system
options.C: To eliminate performance anxiety by removing the pressure of intercourse
options.D: To increase muscular strength in the lower pelvic floor

explanation: Sensate focus helps couples slow down and reconnect through gentle touch, taking away the stressful expectation of sexual performance.

question: Which hormone is primarily responsible for the relaxation of pelvic joints and ligaments during pregnancy?

options.A: Thyroxine
options.B: Relaxin
options.C: Insulin
options.D: Cortisol

explanation: Relaxin works on connective tissue and ligaments to loosen the pelvic girdle in preparation for childbirth. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T003#GNS226_U2_T003_h5)

question: As a nursing student, how should you easily tell the difference between 'morbidity' and 'mortality'?

options.A: Morbidity is a statistic while mortality is a clinical diagnosis
options.B: Morbidity refers to illness while mortality refers to death
options.C: Morbidity affects only infants while mortality affects mothers
options.D: Morbidity is always preventable while mortality is inevitable

explanation: Think of it this way: morbidity means being sick or having health complications, while mortality simply means death. Simple and clear!

question: Which chemical messenger does the sympathetic nervous system release to speed up the heart?

options.A: Insulin
options.B: Norepinephrine
options.C: Bicarbonate
options.D: Acetylcholine

explanation: When your body needs an energy boost or gets stressed, sympathetic nerves release norepinephrine to tell the heart to beat faster and stronger!

question: What are the common signs of a Chlamydia infection in a young female?

options.A: Painless hard sores on the palms
options.B: High fever and generalized skin rash
options.C: Severe joint swelling and stiffness
options.D: Mucopurulent discharge and dysuria

explanation: Spot on! Chlamydia often causes irritation in the cervix and urethra, leading to unusual discharge and painful urination (dysuria).

question: Which healthcare professional do home care nurses often team up with to improve patient mobility?

options.A: Hospital security guards
options.B: Pharmaceutical researchers
options.C: Financial accountants
options.D: Physical therapists

explanation: Physical therapists are fantastic partners! They work alongside nurses to help patients build strength, balance, and safely move around at home.

question: A state health board notices a sharp rise in infant mortality in a rural district through vital data. What action should they take first?

options.A: Increase taxes for citizens living in urban areas
options.B: Close all the primary schools in the affected region
options.C: Stop collecting birth data for the next five years
options.D: Direct more child health resources and immunisation teams to that district

explanation: When data highlights a specific problem area, health planners must channel targeted interventions directly to that community to save lives. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T2#GNS313_U4_T2_h7)

question: Which of these strategies directly helps nurses avoid burnout by giving them more control over their time?

options.A: Mandatory double shifts on weekends
options.B: Flexible scheduling options
options.C: Eliminating all scheduled meal breaks
options.D: Strictly fixed vacation blackouts

explanation: Giving nurses a say in their shifts helps them balance family, rest, and school—a huge shield against burnout!

question: Why does a gishiri cut often result in severe bleeding?

options.A: The instruments used prevent normal blood clotting
options.B: Patients have underlying bleeding disorders
options.C: The vaginal walls and pelvic floor contain a dense network of blood vessels
options.D: Traditional healers use blood-thinning herbs

explanation: The female pelvic region is highly vascular, so blind slashing with sharp blades easily severs major local blood vessels. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T16#GNS312_U1_T16_h3)

question: Why do hydatid cysts often go unnoticed for a long time after infection?

options.A: They dissolve quickly inside the bloodstream
options.B: They grow very slowly over months or years
options.C: They immediately trigger severe immune rejection
options.D: They only affect areas with no nerve supply

explanation: Because these cysts grow so slowly, they stay quiet and hidden for a long time before crowding nearby organs.

question: What does 'psychological safety' mean for a nurse on a hospital ward?

options.A: Being immune from any form of peer review or performance evaluation
options.B: Working night shifts without physical security guards on the ward
options.C: Never experiencing stress or fatigue during clinical duties
options.D: Feeling safe to report errors and speak up without fear of unfair punishment

explanation: You got it! Psychological safety means trust—knowing you can speak up honestly to protect your patients.

question: Which part of the foetal body receives the highest concentration of freshly oxygenated blood?

options.A: The brain and heart
options.B: The gastrointestinal tract
options.C: The lower extremities
options.D: The lungs and trachea

explanation: The foramen ovale directs the freshest, most oxygen-rich blood toward the upper body to support the rapidly growing brain and heart. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T8#GNS121_U6_T8_h4)

question: If a clinic is installing new digital monitors in every patient room, what must be checked first?

options.A: The schedule for the housekeeping staff cleaning the floors
options.B: Adequate electrical outlets and strong wireless network coverage
options.C: The total number of parking spaces available for incoming visitors
options.D: The color of the wall paint and the brand of the room curtains

explanation: Digital gadgets need reliable power and solid Wi-Fi to work properly and show real-time patient updates. Infrastructure must match technology!

question: A patient who previously had a secretive abortion now struggles with recurrent miscarriages in her second trimester. What underlying issue should you suspect?

options.A: Primary ovarian failure due to hormonal imbalances
options.B: Chronic renal failure from past chemical toxicity
options.C: Acquired uterine fibroids from retained tissue
