options.D: Immediately apply a full-thickness skin graft

explanation: Simple, direct pressure with sterile gauze is your best friend for stopping minor bleeding before doing anything else.

question: What do we call that difficult time of year right before the new harvest comes in?

options.A: The drought cycle
options.B: The distribution gap
options.C: The lean season
options.D: The surplus window

explanation: The 'lean season' is when old food supplies have run out and the new crops aren't ready yet. A critical time for community health monitoring!

question: A stroke patient is having trouble swallowing and speaking clearly. Who should you call first?

options.A: Physical therapist
options.B: Orthopedic surgeon
options.C: Social worker
options.D: Speech-language pathologist

explanation: You nailed it! Speech-language pathologists are experts at evaluating and managing speech and swallowing troubles after a stroke.

question: A nurse leader wants to assess the prevalence of needle-stick injuries among nurses in a state hospital to justify safety equipment purchases. Which study design is most appropriate?

options.A: Cross-sectional study
options.B: Case report of a single patient
options.C: Laboratory experiment on bacteria cultures
options.D: Retrospective drug trial over ten years

explanation: Spot on! A cross-sectional survey will quickly reveal how common needle-stick injuries are right now, giving solid proof to demand better safety gear.

question: Which level of cleaning is practically never done inside a regular home care setting?

options.A: Sterilization
options.B: Disinfection
options.C: Cleaning
options.D: Sanitization

explanation: Spot on! Sterilization destroys every single spore and needs heavy hospital equipment like autoclaves—definitely not something you do in a living room.

question: How does a Clinical Decision Support (CDS) feature protect hospitalized patients?

options.A: By printing out paper charts for family members to review at home
options.B: By automatically ordering emergency laboratory tests without doctor approval
options.C: By locking the computer screen whenever a nurse leaves the patient bedside
options.D: By popping up automated warnings about drug allergies or unsafe medication dosages

explanation: CDS tools act as safety nets by analyzing patient data in real time and alerting staff to potential clinical risks before harm occurs. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h3)

question: What is the main job of pulmonary surfactant inside the tiny air sacs (alveoli)?

options.A: To stimulate the diaphragm to contract during inspiration
options.B: To warm incoming air before it reaches the bronchioles
options.C: To transport oxygen directly into the bloodstream
options.D: To lower surface tension and prevent alveolar collapse

explanation: You've got this! Surfactant acts like a special coating that reduces surface tension inside the tiny air sacs, keeping them open and stable so breathing is easy. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T9#GNS213_U2_T9_h1)

question: When would a community health team rely on a sample survey instead of a census?

options.A: When recording a marriage certificate
options.B: When complete registration is not possible
options.C: When every single citizen comes to the clinic
options.D: When the government wants to count every building

explanation: Sample surveys are used to gather reliable estimates from a smaller group when tracking down every single person is too difficult. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T2#GNS313_U4_T2_h2)

question: What is the main job of synovial fluid inside a joint?

options.A: To supply blood vessels directly to the articular cartilage
options.B: To anchor skeletal muscles directly to the bone
options.C: To reduce friction and nourish the cartilage
options.D: To produce white blood cells during an infection

explanation: Spot on! Because cartilage doesn't have its own blood supply, synovial fluid acts like engine oil—bringing nutrients and keeping movements smooth.

question: A patient develops severe belly pain and a hard, rigid abdomen a few hours after a paracentesis. What could this mean?

options.A: Internal bleeding or bowel perforation
options.B: A mild allergic reaction to the dressing
options.C: Normal healing of the puncture wound
options.D: Successful removal of all ascites fluid

explanation: A hard, painful belly is a red flag! It can point to a serious issue like internal bleeding or an accidental nick in the bowel.

question: What is the primary advantage of giving medications through the oral route?

options.A: It bypasses liver metabolism completely
options.B: It is the most convenient and common way
options.C: It guarantees 100 percent drug absorption
options.D: It works faster than intravenous injections

explanation: The oral route is favored because patients can usually swallow pills themselves, making it easy and convenient for long-term care. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T14#GNS122_U1_T14_h1)

question: What happens if money meant for the DRF is used to pay for unrelated hospital bills?

options.A: The prices of medicines in the hospital automatically decrease for all patients
options.B: The pharmacy runs out of stock because money is missing to buy new drugs
options.C: The pharmacy staff must pay for the missing inventory out of their own salaries
options.D: The government automatically replaces the missing funds within twenty-four hours

explanation: Because the DRF relies completely on its own cash flow, taking cash out for other projects breaks the cycle and leaves the shelves empty.

question: What does the term 'bioavailability' mean in nutrition?

options.A: The proportion of a nutrient successfully absorbed and used by the body
options.B: The total percentage of water contained within a specific food item
options.C: The total number of calories released when a food is burned
options.D: The speed at which food travels from the mouth to the stomach

explanation: Correct! Bioavailability just asks: out of all the nutrients you swallowed, how much actually made it into your bloodstream to do work?

question: Which of these is a normal finding and NOT a reason to refer a client to a special clinic?

options.A: Routine spontaneous passage of small lochial blood clots
options.B: Underlying chronic illness requiring careful risk assessment
options.C: History of severe adverse side effects with previous pills
options.D: Desire for long-acting reversible contraception like an implant

explanation: Passing small blood clots early in the postpartum period is totally normal and expected, so it does not need a special referral.

question: What is the main goal of primary prevention?

options.A: To rehabilitate a patient who suffered a stroke or paralysis
options.B: To cure a chronic illness that has lasted for many years
options.C: To prevent a disease from ever occurring in a healthy person
options.D: To screen a community for early signs of high blood sugar

explanation: You nailed it! Primary prevention is all about stopping health problems before they even start by promoting healthy habits and tackling risk factors.

question: How do qualitative and quantitative approaches differ in their main goals?

options.A: Qualitative avoids human subjects while quantitative studies only animals
options.B: Qualitative uses statistical formulas while quantitative uses personal stories
options.C: Qualitative focuses on lab equipment while quantitative focuses on interviews
options.D: Qualitative seeks deep meaning while quantitative seeks prediction and control

explanation: Simply put: qualitative wants to understand the 'why' and 'how' of feelings, while quantitative wants to measure and test facts.

question: What happens when a hospital collects survey feedback from nurses but never actually changes anything?

options.A: Turnover rates drop because staff appreciate being asked
options.B: The hospital saves money on administrative overhead
options.C: Employee motivation automatically increases anyway
options.D: Staff develop cynicism and lose trust in leadership

explanation: If staff share their struggles and nothing changes, they stop caring and lose trust in management. Actions speak louder than surveys!

question: What constitutes a 'shift' on a run chart according to standard interpretation rules?

options.A: Six or more consecutive points on one side of the median
options.B: A single data point that sits extremely high on the graph
options.C: Five or more consecutive points moving in one direction
options.D: Two data points crossing over the median line rapidly

explanation: A shift is defined as at least six consecutive points falling entirely above or entirely below the median line. [learn more](GST319_U1_T3#GST319_U1_T3_h5)

question: What happens when pyrantel pamoate affects a roundworm's nerves and muscles?

options.A: Migration to the lungs
options.B: Spastic paralysis of the worm
options.C: Rapid growth and reproduction
options.D: Enhanced nutrient absorption

explanation: You got it! Pyrantel locks the worm's muscles in a tight paralysis so it loses its grip on the gut wall and gets pooped out.

question: What are the three core action steps of Psychological First Aid?

options.A: Diagnose, Treat, Refer
options.B: Analyze, Process, Cure
options.C: Look, Listen, Link
options.D: Sedate, Calm, Rest

explanation: The three basic action principles of PFA guide helpers to observe safety, listen to needs, and connect people to resources. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T6#GNS315_U5_T6_h6)

question: What is the main reason why nurses conduct research and write proposals?

options.A: To increase the administrative workload of nurses
options.B: Improve patient care and clinical outcomes
options.C: Completely eliminate hospital budgets
options.D: To reduce the number of registered nurses needed

explanation: At the end of the day, everything we do in nursing research is about finding better ways to help our patients heal safely at the bedside.

question: Why are hospital utility bills counted as 'indirect costs'?

options.A: They are shared across the facility and cannot be tied to one patient
options.B: They are paid directly by the nursing department
options.C: They only apply to private hospital rooms
options.D: They change every single day based on the weather

explanation: Things like electricity and water keep the whole hospital running for everyone, so you can't assign them to just one single patient's bill.

question: Which sign strongly points to severe pre-eclampsia in a pregnant mum?

options.A: Painful urination and cloudy urine output
options.B: Itchy skin on the palms and soles of the feet
options.C: Frequent hunger and increased thirst
options.D: Sudden severe headache and high blood pressure

explanation: High BP combined with a terrible headache or vision changes is a classic red flag for severe pre-eclampsia. Keep your eyes peeled for this!

question: What is the main purpose of mobile vaccination clinics and outreach services?

options.A: To bring immunization services closer to remote or hard-to-reach populations
options.B: To provide emergency surgical care during disease outbreaks
options.C: To reduce the number of trained nurses needed in clinics
options.D: To replace permanent hospitals in major cities

explanation: Outreach services overcome distance barriers by bringing vaccines directly to communities that cannot travel to health centers. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T71#GNS214_U1_T71_h5)

question: What makes an intraarterial line different from a standard intravenous (IV) line?

options.A: Medication is delivered directly into an artery
options.B: Infusions are always powered by gravity alone
options.C: Drugs are absorbed slowly through the digestive tract
options.D: Catheters are exclusively placed in the jugular vein

explanation: You've got this! The key difference is right in the name: instead of going into a vein like a normal IV, the catheter goes straight into an arterial blood vessel.

question: Which type of transmission happens when tiny germ particles float in the air over long distances?

options.A: Vector-borne transmission
options.B: Airborne transmission
options.C: Direct contact
options.D: Droplet transmission

explanation: You've got it! Airborne germs are super tiny and can ride the air currents across a room.

question: What is the anatomical term for a joint where two or more bones meet?

options.A: A cartilage bridge
options.B: A ligament anchor
options.C: A bone fusion
options.D: An articulation

explanation: You got this! In anatomy, the official word for where bones meet is an 'articulation'. Think of it as how bones articulate or connect with each other.

question: What is the primary purpose of indirect nursing care technologies?

options.A: To support behind-the-scenes hospital operations and administrative tasks
options.B: To monitor patient vital signs directly at the skin surface
options.C: To replace bedside nurses during surgical procedures
options.D: To diagnose complex diseases without laboratory tests

explanation: Indirect care technologies handle logistics, scheduling, and inventory so that nurses spend less time on paperwork. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T5#GNS113_U4_T5_h1)

question: Why do we perform a crossmatch test before giving a blood transfusion?

options.A: To check for direct reactions between donor cells and recipient serum
options.B: To measure the exact volume of red blood cells in the patient
options.C: To find out if the patient has any hidden infectious diseases
options.D: To determine the patient's baseline hemoglobin and hematocrit

explanation: Crossmatching is a crucial safety step! Lab staff mix donor cells and recipient serum together first to make sure they won't react violently inside the patient's body. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T2#GNS111_U2_T2_h4)

question: Why does the migration of healthcare workers out of rural primary centers severely damage the PHC system?

options.A: It leaves community health facilities understaffed and unable to provide continuous care
options.B: It forces the government to close down all universities in the country
options.C: It increases the cost of building large teaching hospitals in major cities
options.D: It causes patients to stop trusting traditional herbal medicine

explanation: You nailed it! Without skilled nurses on the ground in rural areas, essential services like immunizations, antenatal care, and health education grind to a halt.

question: Your study proves a new handwashing technique cuts down ward infections. Where should you explain how ward nurses can use this daily?

options.A: In the discussion and nursing implications section
options.B: In the abstract summary at the very beginning
options.C: In the methodology and participant selection chapter
options.D: In the raw data tables of the results section

explanation: This is where research meets the bedside—translating your findings into practical steps for everyday nursing care.

question: A nurse washes her hands thoroughly with soap and water before entering a patient's room. Which group of germs is she mostly trying to wash away?

options.A: Resident microbiota
options.B: Systemic pathogens
options.C: Endogenous spores
options.D: Transient microbiota

explanation: Spot on! When you touch door handles or charts, you pick up temporary ('transient') microbes. Handwashing washes those casual hitchhikers right down the drain before you touch your patient.

question: If a patient catches an infection later in life that weakens their immune system, what is this called?

options.A: Primary hypersensitivity
options.B: Innate immune enhancement
options.C: Secondary immunodeficiency
options.D: Active artificial immunity

explanation: When the immune system becomes weak due to later-life factors like infections, environment, or medications, we call it a secondary immunodeficiency.

question: A ward manager notices more patient falls happening. What should they do right after gathering this data?

options.A: Write a brand new job description for the ward clerk
options.B: Ignore the data until the end of the fiscal year audit
options.C: Compare the fall rates against the established hospital safety benchmark
options.D: Immediately fire the nurses working the night shift without investigation

explanation: Once you collect the data, the logical next step is to compare it to your hospital's safety standard to see how big the gap is.

question: Why do adolescent girls need extra iron in their diet?

options.A: To build stronger heart valves
options.B: To compensate for menstrual blood loss
options.C: To accelerate the growth of facial hair
options.D: To prevent the softening of tooth enamel

explanation: Correct! Because of monthly periods, girls lose some iron and need a good diet to keep their blood healthy and prevent anemia.

question: How is true sputum different from ordinary saliva?

options.A: Saliva is thick and colored green or yellow due to infection
options.B: Sputum is produced entirely by glands inside the oral cavity
options.C: Saliva contains high amounts of blood and cellular debris
options.D: Sputum comes from deep in the lungs and lower respiratory tract

explanation: Saliva is just mouth fluid, but sputum comes coughing up from the lungs and bronchial tubes, which is what the lab needs to see.

question: A nurse sees imported vaccines with broken safety seals. Which agency should be alerted immediately?

options.A: The Nigerian Police Force
options.B: National Bureau of Statistics
options.C: NAFDAC
options.D: NMCN

explanation: Great thinking! NAFDAC is our national watchdog for checking the safety and quality of drugs, vaccines, and medical products coming into the country.

question: What happens in the body to cause an erection during sexual arousal?

options.A: Rapid dehydration of the body
options.B: Constriction of the pelvic arteries
options.C: Depletion of adrenal hormones
options.D: Vasocongestion of penile tissues

explanation: Well done! Arousal sends a rush of blood into the spongy tissues of the penis, causing them to fill up (vasocongestion) and create an erection.

question: In Nigeria, what traditional support system has historically cared for most older adults?

options.A: International charity organizations
options.B: The extended family system
options.C: Government-run nursing homes
options.D: Private health insurance agencies

explanation: You've got it! Culturally, our extended family network in Nigeria takes the lead in housing and looking after our aging relatives.

question: An ovarian cancer that is strictly staying inside the ovaries and hasn't spread is at what stage?

options.A: Stage III
options.B: Stage I
options.C: Stage II
options.D: Stage IV

explanation: Correct! Stage I means the cancer is still completely contained within one or both ovaries.

question: Why is the recovery phase just as important as the active response phase?

options.A: It is the only time nurses are legally allowed to administer medications.
options.B: It helps the community rebuild infrastructure and restore long-term health.
options.C: It prevents disasters from ever happening again in the future.
options.D: It replaces the need for any pre-disaster planning or drills.

explanation: Exactly! Recovery is all about long-term healing, fixing damaged buildings, and supporting the mental health of survivors over months or years.

question: Why is the blood-testis barrier (made by Sertoli cells) so important?

options.A: It prevents testosterone from leaking out of the testicular blood supply
options.B: It filters out harmful bacteria coming directly from the external environment
options.C: It speeds up the movement of mature sperm into the vas deferens
options.D: It protects developing sperm cells from being attacked by the body's own immune system

explanation: Because sperm develop later in life, the body's immune system might treat them like foreign invaders! Sertoli cells form a protective wall to keep the immune system away.

question: Who should be part of the team planning safety for a big public event?

options.A: Private security guards and catering staff only
options.B: Only the venue owners and local ticket vendors
options.C: Organizers, police, fire services, and healthcare leaders
options.D: Elected politicians and international press agencies

explanation: Teamwork makes the dream work! Keeping a big crowd safe takes everyone—from event planners to healthcare pros and emergency services.

question: What is the immediate first step to help a patient with acute urinary retention?

options.A: Administering a potent diuretic to stop urine production
options.B: Sending the patient home with oral muscle relaxants
options.C: Starting strong intravenous antibiotics for infection
options.D: Inserting a urinary catheter to drain the bladder

explanation: The urgent goal is to relieve that dangerous pressure right away by passing a catheter to empty the bladder. Spot on!

question: Which official body sets the rules and standards for nursing practice in Nigeria?

options.A: The National Association of Road Transport Owners
options.B: The Nigerian Union of Petroleum Workers
options.C: The Federal Ministry of Works and Housing
options.D: The Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria

explanation: You got it! The NMCN is our main regulatory body guarding the noble nursing profession in Nigeria.

question: What is a major consequence when health workers judge teenagers seeking reproductive advice?

options.A: Adolescents immediately change their behavior and practice strict abstinence
options.B: Young people report the healthcare workers to international health bodies
options.C: Teenagers stop seeking professional help and turn to unsafe alternatives
options.D: Parents take over the health education role completely at home

explanation: Stigma and judgmental attitudes drive vulnerable youths away from clinics, leading to hidden risks like unsafe abortions. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h6)

question: Why might ethical rules stop a nurse researcher from using an experimental design for certain topics?

options.A: Experimental designs always cost more money than hospitals have
options.B: Ethical committees only approve studies written in a foreign language
options.C: Patients refuse to answer questions if a design is experimental
options.D: Researchers cannot intentionally expose human patients to harm

explanation: Patient safety always comes first! If an experiment could put someone at risk, ethics boards require us to use safer, observational designs instead.

question: What is one of the best everyday ways to teach patients to lower their risk of catching STIs?

options.A: Underlining the importance of monthly pelvic ultrasound scans
options.B: Taking daily prophylactic doses of strong broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.C: Avoiding all physical contact with family members in public settings
options.D: Consistent and correct use of barrier methods like condoms

explanation: Barrier methods create a physical block that stops infectious fluids from passing during sex, offering great protection.

question: Why is it important for a nurse to check food and diet instructions before giving an oral medication?

options.A: Eating food stops the liver from performing any first-pass metabolism.
options.B: Food increases the patient's blood pressure and blocks drug excretion.
options.C: Food can bind to certain drugs or alter stomach emptying, changing absorption.
options.D: All oral medications must be mixed with food to prevent severe nausea.

explanation: Food can sometimes block a drug from being absorbed properly or bind to it chemically, making the medicine less effective.

question: What communication style works best to encourage a patient to adopt healthier eating habits?

options.A: A silent demonstration with no words
options.B: A strict and formal medical lecture
options.C: A rapid list of commands to follow
options.D: A collaborative and supportive dialogue

explanation: Working together through supportive conversation helps patients feel empowered rather than judged or forced. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T20#GNS214_U1_T20_h4)

question: How does great community health nursing help ease the burden on big tertiary hospitals in Nigeria?

options.A: By restricting patient movement from rural areas into big cities
options.B: By preventing and treating illnesses early at the local level before they become severe
options.C: By turning primary health centers into major surgical teaching hospitals
options.D: By replacing doctors with nurses in emergency rooms nationwide

explanation: Fantastic! Catching and treating issues early in the neighborhood keeps patients healthy and keeps those big tertiary hospitals from getting too crowded.

question: Which embryonic cells break away to form the peripheral nervous system?

options.A: Endoderm lining
options.B: Surface ectoderm
options.C: Neural crest cells
options.D: Notochord

explanation: You nailed it! Neural crest cells migrate all over the body during development to build our peripheral nerves and ganglia.

question: Which material is most commonly used to make everyday condoms?

options.A: Cotton
options.B: Silicone
options.C: Leather
options.D: Latex

explanation: You got this! Latex is the go-to material for modern condoms because it is strong, stretchy, and reliable at blocking sperm and infections.

question: A nurse is feeling very anxious after a traumatic patient incident on the ward. Where should they turn for immediate, supportive help from fellow health workers?

options.A: The public relations department for media statements
options.B: The legal department for liability review
options.C: A hospital-sponsored peer support team
options.D: The billing office for patient records

explanation: Peer support teams are specially trained to offer a comforting shoulder and an empathetic ear when ward incidents shake your confidence.

question: How do robotic exoskeletons help patients recovering from a spinal injury or stroke?

options.A: By replacing the need for any physical therapy supervision
options.B: By automatically administering intravenous medications
options.C: By permanently curing all forms of neurological paralysis
options.D: By guiding their legs through repetitive walking movements to promote recovery

explanation: Wonderful! Exoskeletons help by moving the legs through steady, repeated steps, which helps retrain the brain and spinal pathways.

question: What is raw data in a hospital setting?

options.A: Finalized hospital financial reports submitted to management
options.B: Unorganized facts and figures collected from clinical observations
options.C: Published research articles found in international medical journals
options.D: Personal opinions shared by senior nurses during ward handovers

explanation: Think of raw data as the raw ingredients! It's just the basic facts and figures gathered straight from the ward before anyone sorts or analyzes them. You've got this!

question: Why do human-made disasters often catch us off guard and create complex challenges?

options.A: They only affect critical infrastructure and leave human populations unharmed
options.B: They strike suddenly without warning and leave behind persistent secondary dangers
options.C: They are easily contained and never require outside medical assistance
options.D: They completely eliminate the risk of subsequent environmental contamination

explanation: Great thinking! Because these events happen without warning and leave behind things like toxic smoke or weak buildings, they keep emergency responders on high alert.

question: Why should a home health nurse spend time checking in on and teaching family caregivers?

options.A: To test the family members on medical terminology
options.B: To protect the caregiver's health and ensure stable care for the client
options.C: To ensure the family takes over all financial costs of the agency
options.D: To replace the primary doctor with a family member

explanation: You got it! Supporting the caregiver keeps them healthy, which means they can keep providing safe, steady care for the patient.

question: What is the main goal of Primary Health Care (PHC)?

options.A: Building specialized tertiary hospitals in every local government
options.B: Bringing essential health care close to where people live
options.C: Training foreign medical doctors for rural service postings
options.D: Providing free medications for chronic non-communicable diseases

explanation: Spot on! PHC is all about bringing basic, necessary health services right to people's doorsteps or communities, so nobody has to travel miles just to see a nurse or doctor.

question: You are nursing a patient undergoing chemotherapy who has a dangerously low white blood cell count. What is your top priority action?

options.A: Practicing strict hand hygiene and enforcing protective isolation measures
options.B: Encouraging the patient to eat fresh, unwashed raw fruits and salads daily
options.C: Avoiding all vital sign checks to prevent disturbing the resting patient
options.D: Allowing large groups of visitors to visit at any time to boost morale

explanation: When white blood cell counts are down, the body's defense shield is lowered. Rigorous hand hygiene and protective isolation are vital to keep everyday environmental germs away from them.

question: Why is a patient told not to eat or drink (NPO) before a laparoscopy?

options.A: To prevent the surgical instruments from getting dirty
options.B: To ensure the patient loses weight before surgery
options.C: To stop the kidneys from producing urine
options.D: To reduce the risk of aspiration during anesthesia

explanation: Spot on! Keeping the stomach empty stops food or vomit from flowing up and entering the lungs while the patient is fast asleep under anesthesia.

question: When wrapping a residual limb with an elastic bandage, where should the pressure be tightest?

options.A: At the bottom end of the stump
options.B: Equally tight all the way up
options.C: Near the top of the joint
options.D: Across the middle portion

explanation: Wrapping tighter at the bottom (distal end) pushes fluid upward and helps shape the limb into a neat cone, which makes fitting a prosthesis much easier later.

question: What is a primary goal of performing a nursing mobility assessment?

options.A: To replace the need for physical therapy input
options.B: To determine functional capacity and plan safe care
options.C: To diagnose underlying genetic bone disorders
options.D: To measure exact daily caloric requirements

explanation: Assessing mobility shows what a patient can safely do on their own and what help they need. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T8#GNS324_U3_T8_h3)

question: Which goal of health spending focuses specifically on making sure poor and vulnerable citizens are not left out?

options.A: Quality assurance
options.B: Cost containment
options.C: Equity
options.D: Privatization

explanation: Think of equity as fairness. It ensures that healthcare resources reach everyone, especially those with lower incomes.

question: Why is building trust so important when giving nutrition advice to outpatients?

options.A: Nurses must legally enforce strict hospital meal schedules
options.B: Clients have autonomy over their daily food choices at home
options.C: Outpatients only eat when supervised by a healthcare provider
options.D: Dietary plans rarely change once the client leaves the clinic

explanation: Spot on! Since outpatients control what they eat at home, having a trusting relationship makes them much more likely to follow your advice.

question: Why must a nurse focus on the ABCDE assessment immediately during suspected anaphylaxis instead of waiting for lab test results?

options.A: Rapid airway closure and shock can cause death within minutes
options.B: Laboratory tests are completely useless for diagnosing allergies
options.C: Skin symptoms always disappear before lab results return
options.D: Hospital protocol forbids drawing blood during emergencies

explanation: Anaphylaxis moves lightning fast. There's no time to wait for lab work when someone's airway is closing up—act first, assess fast!

question: Which infection is most commonly spread when a healthcare worker accidentally suffers a needlestick injury?

options.A: Tuberculosis
options.B: Streptococcus
options.C: Hepatitis B
options.D: Malaria

explanation: Hepatitis B is very easily passed through blood and body fluids. That's why we are always extra careful with needles and sharps in clinicals!

question: Why do public health planners rely on epidemiological data?

options.A: To decide where to direct health resources and programs
options.B: To diagnose individual patients in emergency rooms
options.C: To write personal care plans for recovering clients
options.D: To determine the exact cost of hospital equipment

explanation: Population data helps health authorities see where disease rates are highest so they can build facilities and plan interventions accordingly. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T1#GNS321_U1_T1_h1)

question: How is Ultra-High Temperature (UHT) milk different from standard pasteurized milk?

options.A: UHT milk contains chemical preservatives instead of heat treatment
options.B: UHT milk can remain shelf-stable at room temperature until opened
options.C: UHT milk is boiled slowly on a stove for several hours
options.D: UHT milk requires continuous refrigeration from farm to table

explanation: Brilliant! UHT uses super high heat that wipes out practically all microbes, meaning you can store it on your shelf without a fridge until you pop it open.

question: When a patient is newly connected to a ventilator, what is the most common starting PEEP (Positive End-Expiratory Pressure) setting used to keep small air sacs open?

options.A: 20 cmH2O
options.B: 5 cmH2O
options.C: 0 cmH2O
options.D: 50 cmH2O

explanation: A baseline PEEP of 5 cmH2O acts like a gentle cushion at the end of each breath, stopping tiny air sacs (alveoli) from collapsing so breathing stays easier.

question: Which level of disinfection is needed to reliably kill Mycobacterium tuberculosis on a semi-critical tool?

options.A: Surface sanitization
options.B: Low-level disinfection
options.C: High-level disinfection
options.D: Intermediate-level disinfection

explanation: TB bacteria are tough cookies! You need at least intermediate-level disinfection to knock them out effectively.

question: A community health nurse wants to reach residents who never visit the clinic. What is the best first step?

options.A: Conduct house-to-house surveys and community profiling
options.B: Report the entire community to the federal ministry of health
options.C: Wait patiently in the clinic office for someone to ask for help
options.D: Close the primary health center and move to a big city

explanation: Sometimes patients can't or won't come to the clinic. Going out to meet them through home visits and community mapping is the best way to find those who need help the most.

question: What is another common name for a lumbar puncture?

options.A: Cerebral shunt
options.B: Spinal tap
options.C: Epidural injection
options.D: Bone marrow biopsy

explanation: A lumbar puncture is commonly referred to as a spinal tap because it involves accessing fluid from the spinal column. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T11#GNS222_U3_T11_h1)

question: What happens when a tertiary hospital lacks funds to maintain its intensive care unit?

options.A: The hospital starts generating extra revenue from parking fees
options.B: Patients recover faster by relying on natural rest
options.C: Doctors spend more time teaching medical students
options.D: Critically ill patients experience higher mortality due to broken life support systems

explanation: If ICU equipment and oxygen supplies fail from lack of maintenance, vulnerable patients lose their lives. [learn more](GST322_U4_T2#GST322_U4_T2_h5)

question: What does publishing nursing research primarily help the profession establish?

options.A: Total control over all medical school curricula
options.B: A unique and independent body of knowledge
options.C: The right to practice medicine without a license
options.D: Exemption from hospital ethical oversight boards

explanation: Spot on! Having our own distinct set of scientific knowledge is what truly makes nursing a respected, independent profession.

question: Which of the following women is the best candidate for a planned home delivery?

options.A: A 28-year-old with two normal past births, currently at 39 weeks with a head-first baby
options.B: A mother who experienced a severe heavy bleed after her last delivery
options.C: A 40-year-old carrying twins at 34 weeks who has severe chronic high blood pressure
options.D: A first-time mother whose baby is currently lying completely sideways in the womb

explanation: This mother has a term, single, head-first baby and a history of normal births, fitting all low-risk criteria. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T8#GNS225_U3_T8_h3)

question: What does continuous bubbling in the water seal chamber usually mean?

options.A: An air leak in the system
options.B: Normal lung re-expansion
options.C: High suction pressure levels
options.D: Blocked drainage tubing

explanation: Correct! While a little bit of bubbling can be normal, constant bubbling is a red flag that there's an unwanted air leak somewhere in the tubing or connections.

question: What is the best way to give pain medication to a dying patient in constant pain?

options.A: Around the clock on a regular schedule to prevent pain
options.B: When the family expresses concern about visible discomfort
options.C: Every time the blood pressure drops below normal limits
options.D: Only when the patient specifically asks for relief

explanation: Staying ahead of the pain with a regular schedule keeps the patient comfortable, rather than waiting for them to hurt before reacting.

question: Which of these is a classic example of primary prevention in community health?

options.A: Providing physical therapy after a stroke
options.B: Conducting blood pressure screening for adults
options.C: Treating complications of advanced diabetes
options.D: Administering routine childhood immunizations

explanation: You nailed it! Primary prevention stops diseases before they even start. Vaccines are a fantastic way to protect children proactively before germs ever get a chance.

question: What is the primary direction of time in a prospective research design?

options.A: Moving backward from the present into the past
options.B: Comparing two different time periods in history
options.C: Moving forward from the present into the future
options.D: Examining past medical records for current outcomes

explanation: Prospective studies are designed to follow participants forward in time to observe future outcomes. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T15#GNS224_U1_T15_h1)

question: What shape does the *Vibrio cholerae* bacterium have under a microscope?

options.A: Spherical clusters
options.B: Long branching filaments
options.C: Comma-shaped
options.D: Thick spore-forming rods

explanation: Think of a tiny punctuation mark! Vibrio cholerae is classically recognized as a curved, comma-shaped rod.

question: Why is it important to quickly report and investigate serious adverse events following immunization (AEFIs)?

options.A: To increase the total number of children attending clinic
options.B: To protect public confidence and maintain safety standards
options.C: To eliminate the need for cold chain temperature logs
options.D: To ensure that nurses receive financial compensation

explanation: Acting fast and being transparent stops panic, squashes false rumors, and keeps trust high in our healthcare services.

question: How does foremilk differ from hindmilk during a single feed?

options.A: Foremilk is more watery, while hindmilk contains higher amounts of fat
options.B: Foremilk has high calorie counts, while hindmilk contains only lactose
options.C: Foremilk is produced at night, while hindmilk is produced during the day
options.D: Foremilk contains antibodies, while hindmilk contains only pure water

explanation: Spot on! Foremilk quenches the baby's thirst at the start, while the rich, creamy hindmilk follows to help them grow and feel full.

question: Which of these is NOT something a good nursing research problem should be?

options.A: It must be practically feasible
options.B: It must cause physical harm to test resilience
options.C: It must be significant to patient care
options.D: It must be ethical to study

explanation: Never! As nurses, our golden rule is 'do no harm.' Ethical research will never intentionally cause physical or emotional pain to patients.

question: What is the golden rule of fluid balance when it comes to sodium?

options.A: Sodium ignores fluid shifts
options.B: Water follows sodium
options.C: Sodium follows protein
options.D: Water pushes sodium out

explanation: You got it! Think of sodium as a magnet—wherever sodium goes, water is definitely going to follow it.

question: Which instrument is most commonly used for safe uterine evacuation during PAC procedures?

options.A: Disposable plastic speculum
options.B: Manual Vacuum Aspiration (MVA) kit
options.C: Rigid metal obstetric forceps
options.D: Standard surgical scalpel

explanation: MVA kits use a gentle suction created by a handheld syringe to empty the uterus safely and effectively with minimal trauma to the patient.

question: A patient with uncontrolled chronic hypertension undergoes an ophthalmoscopy. Which finding is the nurse most likely to see documented?

options.A: A completely absent red reflex caused by a dense corneal scar
options.B: Total detachment of the sensory retina away from the back wall
options.C: Bright green pigment spots scattered evenly across the macula
options.D: Arteriovenous nicking where thickened arteries cross retinal veins

explanation: Chronic high blood pressure causes thickening and stiffening of retinal arterioles, leading to the classic sign of arteriovenous nicking. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T8#GNS221_U2_T8_h8)

question: How is the grey matter and white matter arranged inside the developing spinal cord?

options.A: White matter forms internally and gray matter forms externally
options.B: Sensory fibers are kept completely outside the spinal column
options.C: Gray matter forms internally and white matter forms externally
options.D: Motor neurons develop only within the outer white matter

explanation: Great thinking! The spinal cord is neatly organized with nerve cell bodies on the inside (grey matter) and nerve fiber tracts on the outside (white matter).

question: A hospitalized patient has acute salpingitis with pelvic pain and a mild fever. Which nursing position helps drain pelvic fluids downward?

options.A: Ice packs applied directly to the lower abdomen
options.B: Strict bed rest flat on her back
options.C: Trendelenburg position with feet elevated
options.D: Semi-Fowler's position

explanation: Gravity is our friend here! Keeping the patient slightly upright helps infected fluids pool safely in the lower pelvis rather than spreading upward.

question: Which action shows that a nurse is truly practicing active listening?

options.A: Giving full attention and minimizing distractions
options.B: Interrupting to offer quick medical solutions
options.C: Looking around the room for the next client
options.D: Writing in a chart while the patient speaks

explanation: Active listening means putting other tasks aside and showing the patient they have your complete, caring focus.

question: What is the main job of the Peripheral Nervous System (PNS)?

options.A: To act as communication lines linking the body to the CNS
options.B: To process and integrate complex memories
options.C: To produce cerebrospinal fluid for the brain
options.D: To directly control hormonal release in the pituitary gland

explanation: The PNS acts like telephone wires, carrying messages back and forth between your body and the central control unit. You're doing great! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T2#GNS211_U3_T2_h2)

question: Why does the body need to control hormone release very carefully?

options.A: To keep blood volume extremely high at all times
options.B: To replace lost nerve impulses during physical stress
options.C: To ensure the kidneys filter blood at a constant rate
options.D: To prevent chaos in the body and keep things stable

explanation: Too much or too little of a hormone can upset your body's balance (homeostasis). Careful control keeps everything running smoothly!

question: An older adult patient in the ward feels sad about losing their physical strength and independence. Which core emotional need is most challenged here?

options.A: Unconditional parental caregiving
options.B: Financial asset accumulation
options.C: Dignity and a sense of life fulfillment
options.D: Identity exploration and peer acceptance

explanation: Growing older and losing independence can make patients feel vulnerable. Protecting their dignity and helping them feel valued is a key nursing duty.

question: Why can suddenly stopping long-term steroid medications trigger an adrenal crisis?

options.A: Stopping steroids causes the liver to destroy all circulating glucose
options.B: Steroid pills turn into toxic acid inside the stomach lining
options.C: The adrenal glands become lazy and stop making natural cortisol
options.D: The thyroid gland reacts by shutting down body temperature controls

explanation: When you take external steroids for a long time, your adrenals take a break from making their own. If you stop abruptly, they can't bounce back fast enough!

question: Which of these is NOT part of basic respiratory hygiene in a clinic waiting area?

options.A: Placing hand sanitizer dispensers near the entrance
options.B: Mandating full isolation gowns for all visitors
options.C: Providing facial tissues for visitors
options.D: Offering surgical masks to coughing individuals

explanation: Correct! Visitors do not need isolation gowns just to sit in a waiting area. Respiratory hygiene is all about masks, tissues, clean hands, and catching coughs.

question: When is an asynchronous tele-nursing approach most useful?

options.A: When conducting a cardiac resuscitation emergency call
options.B: When sending recorded data or messages for a nurse to review later
options.C: When a patient is actively bleeding and needs immediate instructions
options.D: When performing a live physical examination over video

explanation: Think of asynchronous care as 'store-and-forward.' The patient sends a message or reading, and you check it when you have a moment.

question: Why is it so important to use a client-centered approach during family planning counseling?

options.A: It allows the nurse to choose the most expensive method available
options.B: It stops the client from asking questions about side effects
options.C: It guarantees that the client will choose permanent sterilization
options.D: It ensures the client selects a method that fits her lifestyle and health needs

explanation: Nursing is all about the patient! When a client helps choose her own method, she feels respected and is much more likely to use it correctly.

question: What is the main goal of a community's 'production, distribution, and consumption' function?

options.A: Providing free hospital care to every citizen
options.B: Teaching cultural values to children in school buildings
options.C: Enforcing criminal laws and maintaining local police stations
options.D: Meeting the basic survival and economic needs of members

explanation: You've got it! This is simply about making sure people have access to food, shelter, and the basics needed to survive every day.

question: Why must minor tranquilizers be reduced slowly (tapered) instead of stopping them all at once?

options.A: To ensure the prescription lasts until the next clinic visit
options.B: To allow the liver time to regenerate damaged cells
options.C: To prevent the patient from experiencing immediate weight gain
options.D: To prevent dangerous withdrawal symptoms like seizures

explanation: Stopping suddenly after the body has gotten used to the drug can cause severe rebound anxiety or even seizures. Safety first!

question: How long does the post-natal period (puerperium) typically last in clinical practice?

options.A: Six months
options.B: Two weeks
options.C: Six weeks
options.D: Three months

explanation: You'll see this time and again in midwifery! The post-natal period is officially defined as the first six weeks after childbirth when the mother's body returns to its pre-pregnant state.

question: What is the main purpose of 'organizing' in nursing management?

options.A: Measuring patient health outcomes after discharge
options.B: Arranging resources, roles, and workflows to achieve goals
options.C: Writing the hospital mission statement
options.D: Motivating employees through public praise

explanation: Organizing is about setting up your environment and tools so that your plans can actually happen without stress.

question: Why is it an urgent concern if a child's weight line crosses downward across Z-score lines?

options.A: It indicates normal seasonal weight loss in toddlers
options.B: It means the mother has stopped bringing the child to the clinic
options.C: It shows an active deterioration in nutritional status
options.D: It proves the weighing scale was broken during the visit

explanation: Crossing downward means the child is actively losing ground toward malnutrition and needs quick clinical attention.

question: What is the correct way to apply eye ointment to a newborn?

options.A: Rub the ointment vigorously over closed eyelids until fully absorbed
options.B: Place a large drop directly onto the center of the open cornea
options.C: Flush the entire eye with saline before squeezing ointment onto the iris
options.D: Apply a thin ribbon along the lower conjunctival sac from inner to outer canthus

explanation: Gently draw a thin line of the ointment along the lower eyelid pocket, moving from the inside corner to the outside corner. Simple and safe!

question: What do we call the everyday living conditions, money, and environments that shape a person's health and life choices?

options.A: Social determinants of health
options.B: Biological risk factors
options.C: Physiological markers
options.D: Genetic predispositions

explanation: Spot on! Social determinants are the external things like money, community, and housing that deeply influence our health decisions every day.

question: If a line graph has multiple lines on it, what is the purpose of the legend?

options.A: To show the maximum possible score on the vertical axis
options.B: To explain the mathematical formula used to calculate the average
options.C: To state the name of the hospital where the research took place
options.D: To identify which color or pattern belongs to each specific variable

explanation: Spot on! The legend acts like a key, helping you figure out which line represents which group without guessing.

question: A community health team wants to know if their new malaria prevention posters were successful. What is the best way to check?

options.A: Ask the local printer if they enjoyed making the colorful graphic designs
options.B: Count how many posters are left neatly stacked inside the nurse's office drawer
options.C: Measure changes in community health habits, such as increased use of insecticide-treated nets
options.D: Assume success because the hospital director liked the color scheme

explanation: The real test of good communication is seeing actual behavior change and healthier habits in the community!

question: A nurse manager wants everyone on the ward to share ideas on a new admission form to get their support. Which style is she using?

options.A: Democratic
options.B: Transactional
options.C: Laissez-faire
options.D: Autocratic

explanation: That's democratic leadership! Involving the team makes everyone feel heard and willing to support the new change.

question: Why is a good referral system so important for a client's reproductive rights?

options.A: It gives nurses full authority to choose which contraceptive a client must use
options.B: It forces clients to accept permanent contraceptive methods
options.C: It prevents clients from visiting traditional birth attendants
options.D: It ensures clients can access their preferred method even if local stock runs out

explanation: Clients have the right to choose what works for their bodies. If your clinic runs out of a specific supply, referring them elsewhere protects that choice!

question: What do we call a loss that can be clearly seen and verified by everyone around, like losing a limb or a loved one?

options.A: A loss that is only felt internally by the affected individual
options.B: A loss of money or property caused by economic changes
options.C: A loss that occurs only during old age and natural retirement
options.D: A loss that can be recognized and verified by other people

explanation: Spot on! An actual loss is tangible. It's something both the patient and outsiders can clearly see, touch, or acknowledge, like an amputation or death.

question: What should a nurse do if they inspect a wound and notice the edges are still gaping apart?

options.A: Stop the procedure and notify the medical doctor.
options.B: Irrigate the open area with normal saline and remove them anyway.
options.C: Apply strong adhesive tape across the gap and pull the rest.
options.D: Proceed with removing half of the sutures carefully.

explanation: Gaping edges mean the wound has not healed properly, and removing the support will cause the incision to open completely. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of using a syringe driver in clinical practice?

options.A: To flush blocked intravenous lines rapidly with sterile saline
options.B: To deliver a continuous, controlled amount of medication
options.C: To provide intermittent bolus doses every five minutes
options.D: To measure precise hourly urine output in critical care

explanation: A syringe driver is specifically designed to infuse medications slowly and steadily over a set duration. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T4#GNS212_U4_T4_h1)
